CircularEconomy.label: Circular economy
CircularEconomy.title: From vehicle identification to waste collection and treatment.
CircularEconomy.intro: We develop the applications manufacturers and recyclers use to manage take-back operations: identifying a vehicle, assessing a battery, preparing a pickup, negotiating a price, and generating and tracking documents.
CircularEconomy.positioning: Automakers, repair shops, battery holders, collectors, and recyclers: tools to declare, organize, and track each take-back.

CircularEconomy.dossiersTitle: Three ways to explore our work in detail.

CircularEconomy.audienceTitle: What problem do you need to solve?

audiences.question: What is stopping us from preparing this pickup?
audiences.answer: Battery record, packaging, selected packages, collector, and delivery site: all the necessary information is brought together before the packing list is created.

audiences.question: How can owners and service providers work on the same records?
audiences.answer: A declaration workflow for the network, management interfaces for internal teams, and data exchanges with treatment facilities. Access rules reflect each party’s responsibilities.

audiences.question: What treatment price and logistics cost were agreed?
audiences.answer: Each proposal retains its price components, author, date, and status. The history shows both the terms discussed and those accepted.

audiences.question: Does the record contain the right code, documents, and required signatures?
audiences.answer: EWC codes, battery diagnostics, documents, and waste tracking form statuses are handled within the workflow. Application controls highlight required items and incomplete steps.

audiences.question: What information should be exchanged with existing systems?
audiences.answer: Battery data, status changes, and accepted offers can flow to partner systems through APIs and notifications. Each business object and its access rights are considered when defining the integration.

CircularEconomy.scopeTitle: A focused module or a complete application.

scopeItems.title: Extend an existing tool
scopeItems.text: Does your logistics software work well, but declarations still arrive by email? The project can focus on collecting the information and passing it to that system.

scopeItems.title: Improve a workflow that has become limiting
scopeItems.text: Does your network already use an application? We identify the data, rules, and integrations that must be preserved before extending or replacing the relevant component.

scopeItems.title: Build an end-to-end service
scopeItems.text: Are you setting up a new take-back operation? We can develop the network portal, administration tools, and partner integrations you need.

faqs.question: Is this an off-the-shelf software product?
faqs.answer: We design and develop custom applications. The examples show features we have already built; together, we define which ones meet your needs, which rules to adapt, and which systems to connect.

faqs.question: Do we have to replace our existing tools (ERP, transport, MES, billing, etc.)?
faqs.answer: The first step is to determine what your existing tools already cover. An integration or complementary module may be enough. We review the integration options with your IT teams before agreeing on the scope.

faqs.question: Does the application guarantee regulatory compliance?
faqs.answer: It implements the controls and document exchanges defined for the project. Waste classification, transport rules, and applicable obligations must be validated by the responsible specialists. An EWC code or a Trackdéchets connection alone does not guarantee compliance.

faqs.question: Do you only work with vehicles and batteries?
faqs.answer: These are the sectors illustrated by the projects shown here. For another activity, we examine the similarities and differences in products or materials, stakeholders, documents, transactions, and existing tools. The deciding factor is whether our experience applies to the operations you need to support.

faqs.question: Where does AI fit?
faqs.answer: When a need involves reading documents, extracting information, or assisting with assessments, we can explore an AI component. Not all the features in these guides depend on AI: API-based identification, input rules, and status exchanges already address concrete needs.

CircularEconomy.ctaTitle: Define the scope of a real workflow
CircularEconomy.ctaText: Show us a real workflow, the people involved, and the tools already in place.

dossiers.label: End-of-life vehicles
dossiers.title: Identify the vehicle. Complete the record. Organize take-back.
dossiers.summary: License plate or VIN, retrieved specifications, administrative documents, and interfaces for the take-back network.
dossiers.description: An individual or a repair shop starts by declaring a vehicle. Beyond that form, teams need reliable information, prepared documents, and a request they can pass to the parties responsible for collection. Here are the features we have developed to connect these steps.
dossiers.context: Project example: a vehicle take-back platform with individual and professional workflows connected to an existing management system.

sections.title: Start with a plate or VIN, not an empty record.
sections.navLabel: Vehicle data enrichment by plate / VIN
sections.situation: Enrich a vehicle record from a license plate or VIN: retrieve the available make, model, and specifications from an identification service.
actions: The declarant provides the registration country and the available identifier: a license plate or VIN, the vehicle identification number.
The application queries an identification service and populates the record with the returned specifications.
The user is prompted to complete any required fields that remain empty. Manual entry is available when data cannot be retrieved.
sections.rule: The identification method and required fields vary by country. The integration does not assume that every lookup returns a complete record.
sections.result: A structured vehicle record populated with the available specifications and completed with any missing information.

sections.title: Move the request and its administrative record forward together.
sections.situation: The workflow collects the declarant’s documents, generates the transfer and destruction documents required for the French operations covered, and sends them to the signers.
actions: The workflow brings together the information and documents needed to handle the request.
The team finds these items in the vehicle record rather than in separate exchanges.
The generation and electronic signing of transfer and destruction documents are integrated into the process for the relevant French operations.
sections.rule: Document content and signature steps depend on the country and procedure. The project uses the applicable documents and defines the expected signatories.
sections.result: The request, supporting documents, and signature tracking are linked to the relevant vehicle.

sections.title: Give the network a shared operational tool.
sections.situation: Separate interfaces let individuals and repair shops declare vehicles, authorized treatment facilities track handovers, and program teams monitor network progress.
actions: Separate workflows support individual and professional requests.
Management interfaces let teams and partners track vehicles and handling steps.
Connections to the existing system carry the information needed from declaration and collection through dismantling and final tracking.
sections.rule: The public portal and professional tool serve different purposes. Screens and access rights need to reflect that separation.
sections.result: Vehicle-level tracking and interfaces suited to the people declaring, handling and managing operations.

dossiers.label: Batteries, collection & recovery
dossiers.title: A battery to handle, along with its specifications, constraints, and take-back terms.
dossiers.summary: EWC code, condition and diagnostics, packing lists, treatment and transport prices, receipt, and treatment tracking.
dossiers.description: A battery is more than a reference and a pickup address. Its type, condition, documents, and agreed terms affect how it is handled. We have developed the modules below for recycling and second-life projects.
dossiers.context: Examples from several applications developed for an automotive manufacturer and a battery recycler. The modules are presented together to explain the operations they support.

sections.title: Identify the battery and record its waste code.
sections.navLabel: Battery identification, VIN / BIN and reference data
sections.situation: The declaration combines VIN or BIN identifiers with reference characteristics: model, dimensions, and weight. The holder adds condition, charge, state of health, EWC and UN codes, supporting documents, and photos.
actions: The declaration links the battery to its type and holder information.
The workflow suggests an EWC (European Waste Catalogue) code using the existing declaration or reference battery type.
The declarant can select or correct the code. It is saved in the record, and any changes can be viewed in the history.
sections.rule: Prefilled information comes from reference data. It does not replace validation of the waste classification by the responsible stakeholders.
sections.result: A fully characterized battery record ready for collection, transport, and traceability.

sections.title: Capture battery condition before collection.
sections.situation: The declarant records the battery’s condition and attaches diagnostics, photos, and a checklist. The interface displays the ADR transport information associated with the selected condition.
actions: The declarant records battery condition and attaches the diagnostic and checklist documents required by the workflow.
ADR transport information associated with the selected condition is shown in the interface.
Overview photos are requested, along with a serial-number photo when required based on the declarant and the readability of the identifier.
sections.rule: Required documents depend on context. Transport and packaging rules are defined with the responsible specialists; the portal does not infer them from a photograph.
sections.result: A record bringing together declared condition, photos and documents needed to assess handling.

sections.title: Build a consistent packing list.
sections.situation: The user groups packages from several declarations into a packing list. The application checks collector and destination-site compatibility to prepare a shared shipment.
actions: Users review declarations with their owner, collector, delivery site, chemistry, packaging, and status.
They select the packages to include in the packing list.
In the workflow we developed, the selection controls prevent incompatible delivery sites or collectors from being included in the same group.
sections.rule: This grouping check is an explicit business rule. For your organization, we define the criteria that allow or prevent packages from being shipped together.
sections.result: A packing list linked to declarations, packaging, palletization and the planned transport.

sections.title: Separate the treatment price from the logistics cost.
sections.situation: Providers propose separate treatment and logistics prices, with a currency and comment. Each offer is retained with its author, date, and acceptance or rejection.
actions: A proposal includes the treatment price, logistics cost, currency, and an optional comment.
Each successive proposal is retained with its author, date, and acceptance or rejection status.
Service providers can also manage proposals through an API. Notifications can inform their systems when a proposal is created or accepted.
sections.rule: This example covers price negotiations for batteries and pickup groups. A trading arrangement involving multiple purchase and resale contracts would need to be scoped separately.
sections.result: Proposed and agreed terms remain available with the record, without searching an email chain for the latest agreement.

sections.title: Connect collection, receipt, and treatment.
sections.situation: The application tracks ready-for-pickup, collected, received, and treated stages. Receipt records the date and operator; Trackdéchets exchanges update the waste tracking form in the relevant workflows.
actions: Statuses distinguish batteries that are ready for pickup, collected, received, or treated.
In a workflow connected to Trackdéchets, the receipt step records a date and the recipient’s name, then updates the linked waste tracking form and declaration.
Partners can be notified of status changes to update their own tracking.
sections.rule: Physical and document tracking are linked but remain distinct. The workflow shows the current stage and any actions still required.
sections.result: A declaration tracked after departure from the holder’s site, with the associated steps and documents.
data: Linked waste tracking form, where applicable

dossiers.label: Documents & integrations
dossiers.title: Keep information and documents connected to operations.
dossiers.summary: EWC, ADR, Trackdéchets waste tracking forms, signatures, and API exchanges: what the applications handle and where your systems fit.
dossiers.description: Operations often involve several applications. The business record needs to retain useful references, track document stages, and send events to partners. Here are some of the integrations and controls we have developed.
dossiers.context: Examples from vehicle and battery projects. Document obligations and integration capabilities must be checked for each country, activity and system involved.

sections.title: EWC and ADR: separate information, separate purposes.
sections.situation: Waste classification codes and transport information need to be recorded in the right place. Grouping them under a compliance label does not explain what the tool actually does.
actions: The EWC code is linked to the declaration and can be suggested from the reference battery type.
Battery condition is recorded separately with the required diagnostic documents.
The interface displays the ADR information defined for that condition. Teams define input rules, supporting documents, and required approvals.
sections.rule: The application organizes data and applies defined rules. It does not automatically turn an EWC code into authorization for transport or treatment.
sections.result: Distinct, accessible information that helps qualified stakeholders review the record.

sections.title: Track the waste tracking form with the declaration.
sections.situation: The application creates and updates waste tracking forms through Trackdéchets, monitors producer and collector signatures, and then transmits receipt and treatment information.
actions: The application creates or updates a BSD through Trackdéchets and stores its identifier with the declaration.
It checks the form’s status and distinguishes a missing producer signature from a missing collector signature.
The workflow can make receipt conditional on these signatures, then transmit receipt and treatment information.
sections.rule: A blocked step should explain why and who needs to resolve it. This describes a control in the developed workflow, not a universal legal rule.
sections.result: The form and declaration remain linked; the user sees document status and required actions.

sections.title: Link signatures to the right record.
sections.situation: A document sent for signature should remain connected to the vehicle or operation that generated it.
actions: In the relevant vehicle workflows, transfer and destruction documents are generated within the process.
The DocuSign electronic signature service is integrated into the workflow.
The business record provides access to the documents and signature progress.
sections.rule: Signatories, documents, and signature timing are defined by the procedure. The project also accounts for incomplete steps.
sections.result: The request, prepared documents, and signature status remain connected.

sections.title: Exchange business objects, not just files.
sections.situation: APIs and notifications exchange battery data, price offers, and status changes with providers’ systems. Imports and exports complement these exchanges according to the tools in place.
actions: A service provider API supports battery data imports and exports as well as price proposals.
Outgoing notifications report specific events: a battery assigned, ready for pickup, received or processed; an offer created or accepted.
Access is authenticated and limited to the partner’s scope. Interfaces and exchange formats are defined for the relevant operations.
sections.rule: Integrating with your ERP or logistics software requires an assessment of the available data, direction of exchange, access rights, and error handling. We do not assume that a universal connector exists.
sections.result: A partner can update tracking from its system and receive events relevant to its operations.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.content:
Legal framework – compliance with the GDPR and French law

FDTI Consulting processes personal data in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of April 27, 2016, on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data (hereinafter the GDPR), and with French Law No. 78-17 of January 6, 1978, on information technology, data files, and civil liberties.


The General Data Protection Regulation took effect on May 25, 2018. Organizations that process data must ensure the highest possible level of data protection at all times and be able to demonstrate their compliance through documentation.


Given the nature of its work, FDTI Consulting may need to process personal data collected and processed by its clients. The following provisions define FDTI Consulting's internal processing rules and are intended to ensure that personal data is handled in accordance with the GDPR.


FDTI Consulting considers the protection of personal data fundamental to all its activities. It seeks to anonymize all data it processes as early as possible and works to prevent its disclosure outside the applicable legal frameworks.

Governance

Data processed by FDTI never leaves the European Union and is not subject to any jurisdiction outside the European Union.


Our hosting provider, OVH France, is based in France and hosts our services in France. It is therefore not subject to the CLOUD Act.

Personal data processing

Except in specific cases, FDTI Consulting does not need personal data to perform its services. FDTI Consulting therefore asks its clients not to send it personal data. If FDTI Consulting receives personal data unexpectedly, it will delete the data immediately and notify the sender.


Some personal data may be useful for identification purposes. In such cases, FDTI Consulting will ask the data provider to pseudonymize the data and will assist with the pseudonymization process.

If the sender lacks the technical or human resources to perform this pseudonymization in its own environment, FDTI Consulting will handle it. Only one person within FDTI Consulting will have access to the personal data for the purpose of pseudonymizing it and sharing only the pseudonymized data within FDTI Consulting.


All personal data used in our work is stored securely and processed in accordance with the consent provided by the data subjects. The data is permanently deleted once the studies and processing required for our projects have been completed.

use_case_list.title: Court clerks check filings and judges trace every argument back to its source page
use_case_list.challenge: To review an annual-accounts filing, a commercial court clerk must identify the balance sheet, notes and confidentiality statement, then verify that the fiscal year and figures match across documents. For a trade-register filing, they cross-check declared data against articles of association and deeds. Judges face a different hurdle: finding each party’s claims and supporting arguments across multiple briefs and exhibits.
use_case_list.approach: We built a document-analysis API integrated into the court registries’ line-of-business software alongside a web application, hosted on the software vendor’s servers. The core challenge was handling heterogeneous scanned bundles while keeping every legal assessment in human hands. For annual accounts, the engine classifies submitted documents and selects from more than 50 checks those applicable to the filing so clerks see what matches, what conflicts and what needs manual review. For court cases, it structures facts, claims and arguments by party with source page references.
use_case_list.impact: Deployed across around fifty commercial courts, the platform processes nearly 40,000 filings per month. Inside their usual software, clerks go straight to the checks and discrepancies to settle before validating a filing, and this structured framework has helped registries harmonize their review practices. Preparing a hearing, judges cross-check the summary against the parties’ submissions with exact page references.

details.title: Send the filing

details.title: Verify trade-register deeds

details.text: For sole-trader registrations, it separates identity, address and non-conviction records and groups the corresponding checks.

indexCard.proof: Up to 50 files per batch upload
indexCard.note: Built to handle 3,000 incoming records a month without opening each file manually.

use_case_list.title: File supporting documents for multiple vehicles from a single batch upload
use_case_list.challenge: Within the end-of-life vehicle EPR (extended producer responsibility) scheme, the administrative team receives and scans thousands of paper records every month. Scanned files land together on a workstation even when they belong to different vehicles. To file a registration certificate or a purchase-declaration receipt, the administrator has to open the scan, read the VIN, look up the vehicle, open its record and pick the document type, one file after another.
use_case_list.approach: We built a batch upload and filing module inside the line-of-business application used to manage end-of-life vehicle EPR files. The main challenge was handling uneven garage scan quality while ensuring no document is ever attached to the wrong vehicle or overwritten silently. For each file in the batch, the OCR engine extracts the text, detects the vehicle identification number (VIN) and proposes both the document category and the matching vehicle record in a side-by-side review queue.

details.title: Upload the scan batch
details.text: She drops scanned files together in one batch, even when registration certificates and receipts belong to different vehicles.

details.title: Read type and VIN
details.text: For each file, the module extracts the text, locates the VIN and proposes the recognized document category.

details.title: Match the vehicle file
details.text: It looks up an exact VIN match within the authorized scope and flags missing, ambiguous or unreadable numbers.

details.title: Review side by side
details.text: Next to the original document preview, she checks the proposed vehicle and category or selects another record if needed.

details.title: Confirm without overwriting
details.text: She confirms the attachment; if a document of the same type already exists on the file, a warning appears first.

use_case_list.impact: Instead of repeating vehicle lookups file by file after scanning, the administrator works through a single batch review queue and focuses on unreadable VINs or potential duplicates. Across end-of-life vehicle EPR records, each file receives the validated supporting document without silent overwrites.

use_case_list.title: Prepare compensation schedules and justify every single amount
use_case_list.challenge: In mass-tort proceedings involving thousands of claimants, the judicial team must prepare compensation schedules in which every row maps to the right person. Yet PDF court rulings, spreadsheets submitted by counsel and expert assessments format names and amounts differently. Whenever names overlap or a party amends its claim, the team must trace the source document and explain the figure retained.
use_case_list.approach: We built a dedicated web application for the judicial team preparing compensation schedules, hosted on the client’s own infrastructure. The main challenge was reconciling PDF rulings with shifting lawyer spreadsheets while keeping an audit trail of every human decision. The application extracts data from rulings, imports workbooks while preserving original rows, proposes person-level matches, converts foreign-currency claims using dated official exchange rates, and exports editable Word schedules ready for the judgment.
use_case_list.impact: Running in production on a collective case, the judicial team completed individual review of nearly 250 complex files. For every row in the preparatory schedules, the team can trace the source filing, the expert assessment, the initial claim, the retained figure and the reason for any adjustment when drafting the judgment.

metrics.label: People in source rulings
metrics.note: Individuals listed across the court decisions used for cross-referencing.

metrics.label: Currencies supported
metrics.note: Dated official exchange rates retrieved for foreign-currency claims.

metrics.label: Complex cases reviewed individually
metrics.note: Individual file reviews completed by the team on a collective case.

details.title: Extract and import
details.text: It reads PDF court rulings and imports counsel spreadsheets while keeping every original row accessible in context.

details.title: Resolve person matches
details.text: They review proposed cross-source links and handle namesakes, name changes and uncertain matches separately.

details.title: Record reasoned adjustments
details.text: They weigh claims against expert assessments; whenever an amount is adjusted, both the initial value and the stated reason remain on record.

details.title: Convert and compute
details.text: It calculates each head of loss and retrieves dated official exchange rates for claims submitted in foreign currencies.

details.title: Export judgment schedules
details.text: They export itemized rows and summary totals as editable Word tables ready to insert into the drafted judgment.

indexCard.title: Prepare compensation schedules and justify every single amount
indexCard.description: The same individuals appear across court rulings, counsel spreadsheets and expert assessments. The application reconciles those sources, preserves reasoned adjustments and generates the judgment schedules.

use_case_list.title: From take-back to certificate, an EPR operator tracks every end-of-life vehicle
use_case_list.challenge: To bring an end-of-life vehicle EPR (extended producer responsibility) scheme into compliance, the garage declaring a car, the carrier picking it up and the center receiving it must work from the same file. A car can already sit in the yard while its registration document is still at the garage. The professional back office tracked network take-backs, but opening the service to private owners meant linking their requests to that system, equipping drivers and delivering signed certificates.
use_case_list.approach: We built a take-back portal for private owners and a mobile web application for carriers, connected them to the .NET back office already used by garages and treatment centers, and extended that core system. The key challenge was keeping a single file per vehicle while separating the events each party needs: declaration, pickup, physical arrival in the yard and receipt of administrative paperwork. For the French EPR scheme, we also connected the vehicle file to registration services and electronic signature of transfer and destruction documents.
use_case_list.impact: The platform runs in production for both professionals and private owners and underpins end-of-life vehicle EPR traceability. Garages know when pickup has taken place, treatment centers see which registration documents are still missing, and owners get proof for their insurer. Across the network, physical arrival, administrative paperwork and destruction certificates stay tracked separately.

use_case_list.title: A carmaker routes and tracks every end-of-life battery in its EPR scheme across Europe
use_case_list.challenge: Across the European network of one of the world’s leading carmakers, dealerships, dismantling centers and plants remove traction batteries. Each one must go to the right outlet, to a service provider in the same country, with the required packaging and documents. The routing rules are specific to the carmaker and vary from one battery to the next. To bring its battery EPR (extended producer responsibility) scheme into compliance, the carmaker must be able to say, battery by battery, what became of it.
use_case_list.approach: We designed, built and operate the web platform that runs the carmaker’s battery EPR scheme. It brings together battery holders, collection and treatment providers and the carmaker’s teams. Each battery has a single file: identification by vehicle or battery number cross-checked across several carmaker reference systems, condition, photos, packaging, prices, documents and a time-stamped history. A rules engine applies the carmaker’s policy to select the destination and the provider; the cases defined by the rules go through validation by the carmaker’s team. Providers work in the platform or from their own software, through an API and webhooks. A marketplace sells the lots intended for second life. The interface is available in seven languages.

details.title: Declare the battery
details.text: They enter the vehicle or battery number, record condition, charge and health, then add photos and packaging or import a batch from Excel.

details.title: Route the battery
details.text: The rules engine applies the carmaker’s policy to select the outlet and the provider. The cases defined by the rules go through validation by the carmaker’s team.

details.title: Price and pick up
details.text: The provider proposes its treatment and transport price, which the other party accepts or declines. Batteries from the same site leave in a single pickup.

details.title: Track through treatment
details.text: It records the pickup, the receipt and then the treatment. Each step notifies the holder and the carmaker; the treatment certificate joins the file.

details.title: Work from its own software
details.text: A connected provider re-enters nothing: the platform sends it the battery and the statuses from its tool come back to the file, recycling certificate included.

details.title: Sell second-life lots
details.text: The team builds a lot per site, chooses the admitted buyers and the bidding window, then selects an offer priced in total, per kWh or per kg.

use_case_list.impact: The platform is in production across 19 European countries and underpins the compliance of the carmaker’s battery EPR scheme: for each battery, the team finds the chosen outlet, the provider, the pickup, receipt and treatment dates, and the certificate that attests to them. More than 500 dealerships, dismantling centers, plants, providers and buyers operate on it, and more than 5,500 batteries have a confirmed treatment. North American plants also declare second-life modules on it, and buyers in Europe and Asia bid on the lots.

use_case_list.title: From garage to treatment plant, a recycler tracks every battery in the EPR scheme
use_case_list.challenge: In the battery EPR (extended producer responsibility) scheme, the recycler must be able to explain what arrived at its sites and what was actually treated. Yet the garage knows the battery’s condition, the collector knows where it picked it up and the plant measures what it accepts. The packing list states what should arrive; it is not enough to justify the weight received or the treatment of a battery.
use_case_list.approach: We built for the recycler a web application that links holders’ declarations, pickups and receipts at the plant. To bring the EPR scheme into compliance, it keeps the link between the battery, its waste tracking form and its recycling certificate. It also takes in the declarations sent by a carmaker’s battery platform. The recycler checks the contract and the preliminary acceptance in it; the collector prepares deliveries and checks pickups on a phone. The connection to Trackdéchets, the French national waste tracking service, brings the decisions signed at destination back into the file.

details.title: Declare the battery
details.text: They identify the battery, describe its condition and packaging, and give the pickup location. Declarations from a carmaker’s platform arrive already filled in.

details.title: Accept the battery
details.text: The recycler checks the contract or the accepted offer and the preliminary acceptance certificate, which it can have corrected before signing it.

details.title: Pick up on site
details.text: The driver scans the label from a phone or enters the reference, checks the battery’s record and confirms the collection.

details.title: Prepare the delivery
details.text: They gather the available packages on a packing list. The application leaves out those bound for another site, adds up the weight and offers delivery slots.

details.title: Receive, then treat
details.text: The site records the date and the quantities accepted or refused. When treatment is signed in Trackdéchets, the application generates the recycling certificate.

use_case_list.impact: More than 200 garages, dealerships and depollution centers have already declared more than 1,500 batteries on the platform, from more than 250 collection locations. For its monthly EPR scheme declaration, the recycler’s team reuses the receipt data: originating site, arrival date and weighed weight. For each battery, it distinguishes the receipt form from the certificate that attests to the treatment.

use_case_list.title: Public lighting managers track incidents cabinet by cabinet
use_case_list.challenge: A cabinet is still drawing power in broad daylight. Is it a clock offset, on-site work or consumption that continues after switch-off? For a public lighting manager who looks after several municipalities, the invoice total cannot settle it. They need to find the cabinet, know when its consumption changed and check whether the gap recurs before requesting an on-site inspection.
use_case_list.approach: We built a web application for public lighting managers. It brings together meter readings, switch-on schedules and billing data. The manager selects an area or a group of municipalities and sees on a map the cabinets showing an anomaly. For each one, they can compare several nights, examine the power drawn every half hour and find its address. They also choose the alerts they want when a fault is detected or when readings return to normal. To prepare a contract review, they find for each cabinet the subscribed power, the billed consumption and the average price per kilowatt-hour.
use_case_list.impact: The application tracks more than 6,000 metering points across some sixty lighting networks, mostly municipal. The manager can tell the contractor which cabinet to check, at what time consumption changed and for how many days the gap has appeared. After an intervention, they find the same meter’s readings to see whether the fault is still visible. Energy teams rely on the same references to examine an invoice or review a subscription.

use_case_list.title: Compare campaign themes and tones for an NGO across nine markets
use_case_list.challenge: An international environmental NGO runs awareness campaigns across multiple countries. Its teams can see how many people viewed, commented on or shared a Facebook or Instagram post, yet platform metrics never tell whether a message states a problem, calls for action or quotes a scientist. Preparing upcoming campaigns requires comparing like-for-like messages from one market to the next.
use_case_list.approach: We built a language-model classification pipeline that ingests Facebook and Instagram exports, qualifies every post and outputs enriched spreadsheets directly usable by the communications team. The core challenge was reconciling mismatched export schemas and validating classification accuracy before batch processing. Guided by annotated examples and a review interface, the model records the campaign theme, tone, featured voice and key message right alongside reach and engagement metrics.
use_case_list.impact: Across two years of campaigns, international and local teams share a common framework covering more than 18,000 posts in nine markets. On topics such as ocean protection or climate, they separate heavily posted themes from those driving genuine engagement and pick the angles to test next.

use_case_list.title: Pinpoint what drives a low satisfaction score after an online purchase
use_case_list.challenge: After buying online or setting up a device, customers leave a satisfaction score and a free-text comment. For the customer insights team of a consumer electronics manufacturer, the score alone never tells what needs fixing: a buyer may like the product while penalizing a declined card or a late parcel. Reading and tagging responses by hand across dozens of separate surveys cannot keep up.
use_case_list.approach: We built an ingestion pipeline and a Google Cloud data warehouse for the insights team, bringing together post-purchase survey responses and product reviews alongside a semantic text-analysis module. The key challenge was flattening nested questionnaires sent at different stages after purchase, deduplicating product reviews across catalog variants, and separating text sentiment from the numerical score. The module groups varied phrasings under business topics and surfaces them in Tableau right down to the original verbatim.
use_case_list.impact: The customer insights team works from a unified base of more than 85,000 post-purchase responses and traces score shifts directly to concrete customer verbatims for e-commerce, logistics, product and support teams without reading each survey manually.

details.title: Gather surveys and reviews
details.text: Twice a week, Airflow pulls post-purchase survey responses and online product reviews while preserving score, date and product reference.

details.title: Normalize and deduplicate
details.text: Nested survey payloads are structured in BigQuery and matched to the product catalog while filtering out duplicate reviews.

details.title: Group by meaning
details.text: The model clusters different phrasings of the same issue—such as card failure and checkout rejection—and scores text sentiment separately.

details.title: Drill into a topic
details.text: In Tableau, they filter a period or theme—payment, delivery, product quality or support—and read the underlying customer comments.

details.title: Refine the taxonomy
details.text: Using ambiguous cases spotted during review, the team sharpens its topic definitions, separating late parcels from lost deliveries.

use_case_list.title: A retailer migrates its data warehouse and unifies sales, stock and logistics
use_case_list.challenge: While switching management software, a retailer with more than 500 stores needed to migrate its data warehouse and keep sales, stock, order and shipment reporting running without interruption. Yet the exchanged payloads are large nested JSON objects defined by complex XML schemas: a receipt holds multiple lines, an item multiple descriptions, and past sales must stay tied to the catalog and store as they stood on the purchase date.
use_case_list.approach: We designed for the retailer’s BI team the migration to the new Snowflake data warehouse and the live mapping pipeline ensuring continuity across more than 70 business objects: receipts and payments, items and promotions, stores and staff, stock, orders, goods receipts, shipments and supplier invoices. The core challenge was flattening large nested JSON payloads into relational tables while reconstructing every join. Our generator parses each object’s structured XML specification to automatically produce more than 250 Snowflake tables alongside the unnesting and incremental loading scripts.
use_case_list.impact: The migration ensured a seamless transition to the production data warehouse for sales and logistics teams. Analysts track every store without rebuilding receipts or joins from nested JSON payloads, and catalog reclassifications no longer distort historical comparisons. Whenever a new XML-described object is added, the generator builds its tables and conversion scripts.
